'''''Encephalartos laevifolius''''' is a [[species]] of [[cycad]] that is found in the [[KwaZulu-Natal]], [[Mpumalanga]] and [[Limpopo]] provinces of [[South Africa]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tropicos.org/Name/9600069|title= Encephalartos laevifolius in Tropicos}}</ref> and at [[Piggs Peak]] in [[Eswatini]]. The species is facing extinction in the wild, but is widely cultivated. As of 2012, the ''Encephalartos laevifolius'' has been listed as critically endangered by the IUCN.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Non-determinant finding for Encephalartos Laevifolius|url=https://www.environment.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/nondetrimentfinding_encephalartos_laevifolius.pdf|website=Department of Environmental Affairs}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> 

==Description==
[[image:Encephalartos laevifolius furnas 2015.jpg|thumb|left|Young specimen in the Terra Nostra Garden, [[Povoação, Azores|Azores]]]]
This cycad is tree-like, growing up to 3.5 meters tall with a stem diameter of 25-35 cm. It sometimes develops additional stems from suckers at its base. Its pinnate leaves can reach 1 meter in length, supported by a 22-25 cm long petiole. Each leaf is made up of many pairs of lanceolate, leathery leaflets that are 12-15 cm long, with smooth edges and a sharp tip. This species is dioecious, with male plants bearing 1 to 5 cylindrical-fusiform cones, 30-40 cm long and 9-10 cm wide, in yellow to brown hues. Female plants produce 1-5 cylindrical cones, 20-30 cm long and 10-15 cm wide, in a light yellow color. The seeds are roughly oval-shaped, 2.5-3.5 cm long, and covered with a yellow-orange [[sarcotesta]].<ref name="PlantZAfrica u525">{{cite web | title=Encephalartos laevifolius | website=PlantZAfrica | url=http://pza.sanbi.org/encephalartos-laevifolius | access-date=2024-01-03}}</ref>
